angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,291 km at 158.79 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2975 +/- 0.0157 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 158.79 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.63 +/- 0.01 solar radii from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-338 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 438,291 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.66 +/- 0.02 solar masses from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-338 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4558 +/- 91 K from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-338 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-338 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-338.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.659, rounded to two decimals

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-338 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.83644, from Pope et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.461.3399P/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 656201703533465088, flags_flame 00: age_flame 9.067896 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 5.7404556 to 12.346608)
